title: Canonical finite diagonal class and trace comparison
statement: Let R be a commutative condensed coefficient and A a finite commutative ring. Let Y be Noetherian, and let the positive integer N kill A and be invertible on Y and the diagonal surface. Given a diagonal diagram over R as in [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-category], realizations of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-finite-realization] on Y, its projective line and diagonal surface, and two specified line isomorphisms to the positive finite Cartier lines of [def-sfb-geo-cartier-interface], define their canonical finite comparison property to mean that the following data and equations exist. The supported-source isomorphism is the direct image of the coefficient-unit comparison, normalized on underlying sheaves. The entire diagonal arrow becomes the canonical class of [def-sfb-geo-cartier-canonical-class]. Its finite right-derived projective-line model equals the canonical functor and has the full canonical universal unit. The realization/direct-image square is fixed by the universal unit. The specified splitting has hom exactly the positive unit/Chern splitting of [sk-lem-geo-p1-cohomology], and the trace equation uses its inverse followed by the constant summand projection and the canonical shifted line endpoint of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-quotient-line]. These are comparison data, not an assertion of their existence for every diagonal diagram.
